label: Hardy Deciduous
examples: Maple, Elm, Hornbeam, Beech, Oak, Zelkova, Apple, Crabapple, Larch
description: Trees that drop leaves and need winter dormancy

tasks.title: Structural Pruning
tasks.desc: Best visibility. Remove crossing, co-dominant stems. Always cut to branch collar.
tasks.warning: Japanese Maples bleed if pruned late - do early Feb.

tasks.title: Repot
tasks.desc: Repot as buds swell, before leaves open. Standard soil: 50% akadama, 25% pumice, 25% lava.
tasks.warning: Beech max 20% root removal. Larch repot first - earliest to wake.

tasks.title: Clip & Grow / Pinch
tasks.desc: Let shoot grow 5-6 leaves, cut back to 2. Builds fine ramification.

tasks.title: Defoliation (Optional)
tasks.desc: Strong trees only: remove large outer leaves to force smaller second flush. Partial for Japanese Maple.
tasks.warning: Never defoliate weak tree. Never after mid-July.

tasks.title: Fertilize
tasks.desc: Start organic fertilizer after first leaves harden. Every 2 weeks until mid-Aug.
tasks.warning: Stop nitrogen mid-Aug to harden for winter.

tasks.title: Winter Storage
tasks.desc: Store at 0-4C: unheated garage/shed. Mulch pot, protect from wind/sun.
tasks.warning: Needs 800+ chill hours. Never bring indoors to house.

species_notes.Larch: First to need repot in spring
species_notes.Oak: Prune late winter to reduce bleeding

label: Conifer - Two-Flush Pines
description: Pines that grow twice a year - CRITICAL different care

tasks.title: Repot
tasks.desc: Repot as buds move. Keep 30% old soil for mycorrhizae (white fungus).
tasks.warning: Never bare root. Needs mycorrhizae to live.

tasks.title: CANDLE CUTTING - Key Task
tasks.desc: Cut strong candles short (1/3 left), medium half, weak leave alone. Balances energy.
tasks.warning: TIMING CRITICAL. Too early/late = no second flush.

tasks.title: Old Needle Pull
tasks.desc: Pull last year's old needles to let light/air inside.

tasks.title: Fertilize Heavy
tasks.desc: Heavy spring feed to build strength. Stop 2 weeks before candle cut, resume 2 weeks after.

label: Hardy Evergreen Conifers
examples: White Pine, Scots Pine, Mugo Pine, Spruce, Juniper, Cedar
description: One growth flush per year - do NOT candle cut

tasks.title: Repot
tasks.desc: Repot early-mid spring. Gentle root work. Juniper repot late March-April.
tasks.warning: Juniper never bare root all at once.

tasks.title: Prune to Shape
tasks.desc: For White/Scots/Mugo: AFTER needles harden late June/July, cut back to side buds. For Juniper: pinch tips to balance.
tasks.warning: Do NOT candle cut like Black Pine - will kill bud.

tasks.title: Bud Selection
tasks.desc: At each whorl, remove extra buds leaving 2 sideways. Prevents ugly whorls. For Juniper: thin dense pads for light.

tasks.title: Winter Protection
tasks.desc: Needs cold dormancy but protect pot. Bury pot in mulch, windbreak, out of winter sun. NEVER indoors.
tasks.warning: Number 1 killer of Juniper is keeping indoors in winter.

species_notes.Juniper: Energy in foliage - never strip all tips

label: Tropical / Subtropical
examples: Ficus, Jade, Brazilian Raintree, Fukien Tea, Serissa, Bougainvillea
description: No dormancy, needs warmth. Indoors in winter for cold zones

tasks.title: Move Outdoors
tasks.desc: Move outside after last frost. Ficus needs >12C nights, others >15C. Acclimate to sun over 7 days.
tasks.warning: Direct sun after indoor winter burns leaves - shade first.

tasks.title: Heavy Prune & Style
tasks.desc: Hard prune, full defoliation okay for Ficus if healthy. This is when you build structure.

tasks.title: Repot Tropicals
tasks.desc: Repot in July when hottest and growing fastest. Opposite of hardy trees. Ficus can be bare rooted.
tasks.warning: Serissa only 20% root prune, hates heavy work.

tasks.title: Move Indoors
tasks.desc: Bring indoors under grow lights 14-16hr, humidity tray, 18-22C. Check for spider mites first.
tasks.warning: Spray with insecticidal soap before bringing in.

tasks.title: Indoor Winter Care
tasks.desc: Maintenance only. Water when slightly dry. Light pinch. No heavy work. Leggy growth = needs more light.
tasks.warning: Don't try to build ramification indoors - just keep alive.

species_notes.Ficus: Can take hard prune and bare root
species_notes.Raintree: Leaves close at night - normal, not dying
